title: Focus View — the propagation lens, ported and re-shadcn'd
summary: SystemSketch's bounded upstream/downstream propagation-focus lens, ported into bbox-ui's own scene/editor split: the pure graph traversal moves into scene/focus.ts, the floating toolbar becomes the first file in a brand-new editor/ kit, and its two range inputs are now the vendored shadcn Slider instead of a bare <input type="range"> — Zach's one explicit change on this pass.
branch_label: focus-view-2026-09-18 (isolated lane worktree, cut from claude/bar-block-storybook-e61a36 @ 8064ab6)
intro: Zach's own words, quoted with citations — found in the vault per this task's ask. The immediate brief (/home/bam/zach_brain/Projects/bbox-ui/PROJECT - Black Box UI.md:3130-3145, "The focus slider", Sep 18 2026): "We did a lot of nice work with the actual design of the slider. We made the left slider flipped for example... One thing I would change this time is to make sure we are using Shadcn components. There is the pure functional code that can go in scene with regards to like calculating the graph traversal to see which nodes and edges to highlight/focus and then there is the floating toolbar that should go inside editor components."

The design intent behind the lens, from the original SystemSketch build session (Sources/Chats/Codex/2026-09-04 — 01a06b0a (CHAT).md:6112, transcribed from the Plaud voice note): "...you click on focus flow... I would just show, kind of have the thing centered and then on each side maybe put a slider where I can just quickly drag it as much as I want from 1 to basically the maximum number of steps that you can kind of just pre-calculate ahead of time... once I do focus, I should just be like sliding it, basically is the thing."

The RTL correction itself — this is the feedback the donor code's own WHY comment traces back to, and it is more precise than the "left slider flipped" summary: (Sources/Chats/Codex/2026-09-04 — 01a06b0a (CHAT).md:6651) "Please see my feedback here for the propagation focus sliders. you should flip slider direction of input, show range (1 to max steps) and show current number of steps" — and its landing, two hundred-odd lines later at :6941: "The propagation slider correction is now visually reworked too: each horizon has a real drag runway rather than a tiny thumb control, while retaining the outward RTL/normal directions."

No contradiction found between that feedback and the donor code — propagationGraph.ts/propagationFocus.ts/PropagationFocusControls.tsx already implement exactly what these three quotes ask for (RTL flip, a range display, a current-count display), so this port carries the decision forward rather than resolving a conflict.
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/focus.ts — new: the pure traversal (focusReachableDepth, walkFocus) ported near-verbatim from SystemSketch propagationGraph.ts (134 lines), plus the seed/step-limit/snapshot POLICY re-expressed from propagationFocus.ts's Editor-bound half over a plain BlockScene + seed id (no shape lookups, no store)

apps/storybook-basics/src/scene/focus.test.ts — new: 14 tests — propagationGraph.test.ts's walkPropagationGraph suite ported verbatim (field renames only), plus new coverage for the re-expressed step-limit/snapshot policy

apps/storybook-basics/src/components/slider.tsx — new: the stock shadcn new-york Slider vendored over @base-ui/react/slider, exactly the tooltip.tsx/popover.tsx convention (header names the upstream source, only the cn import path changed)
apps/storybook-basics/src/editor/README.md — new: the editor/ kit's own charter — the third kit alongside components/ and scene/, created for the first time by this ask

apps/storybook-basics/src/editor/focusControls.tsx — new: the floating toolbar, ported as POLICY from PropagationFocusControls.tsx (169 lines) — no tldraw import, takes callbacks and plain data as props so the same toolbar mounts over any host; the RTL upstream range now uses @base-ui/react/direction-provider's DirectionProvider (this Slider is composed, not a native <input>, so a bare dir attribute does nothing to it)

apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/FocusView.stories.tsx — new: 4 stories over a story-local chain+fan-in/fan-out scene, following Lint.stories.tsx's DOM-measured-Trace pattern — 2 interactive (the traversal proof, the RTL-keyboard proof) and 2 pre-seeded capture-only states for this report's screenshots
docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — added the focus.ts row (class (a)+(b), full donor citation)
findings: Baseline measured before touching anything: tsc clean, 38 unit-test files / 721 tests, 59 story files / 258 stories. After: tsc clean, 39 files / 735 unit tests (+14, all in focus.test.ts), 60 story files / 262 stories (+4, all in the one new FocusView.stories.tsx) — every existing file/test count otherwise unchanged.

The traversal claim is asserted twice in the same play function: first directly against focusSnapshot(SCENE, "seed", 2, 1) with no rendering involved at all (exact node/edge id sets, both inclusion and exclusion), then against the live DOM after driving the real toolbar (click seed -> Focus -> ArrowLeft on the upstream slider) — both agree.

The RTL claim is its own story and is BEHAVIORAL, not structural: focus the upstream thumb, press ArrowLeft, assert the value INCREASES (matching the donor's WHY: RTL keeps the direction honest instead of a paint-only flip that would pass a DOM-presence check but fail exactly this). Verified failing first with the story unwritten is not possible without an editor kit at all, so the mutation check instead was: comment out DirectionProvider (plain LTR) and re-run this story alone — it failed exactly as predicted (ArrowLeft decreased the value); restored and it passes again.

Owed wiring, real gap #1: the vendored slider.tsx's own <Slider> convenience wrapper does not forward aria-label/aria-valuetext to the underlying SliderPrimitive.Thumb (only Root gets the spread props) — verified by reading SliderThumb.mjs's own aria-label plumbing, which takes it as ITS OWN prop, not inherited from Root. FocusControls passes aria-label/aria-valuetext to <Slider> anyway (lands on the wrapping group, still useful context) and additionally wraps each range in a <label> (the donor's own technique — its <input> was native, wrapping still works here since Base UI's Thumb renders a real input under the hood), but a screen reader will not get the crisp 'Upstream propagation steps' name today. Real fix needs a second Slider variant (or a thumbProps passthrough) in slider.tsx — a change to a stock, verbatim-vendored file, which is exactly the kind of edit this task's provenance rule says not to make silently.

Owed wiring, real gap #2: this port does not include propagationFocus.ts's tldraw-bound store/subscription/MutationObserver DOM-lens half (the WeakMap<Editor,...> store, connection-admission filter, live-reconciliation-on-selection-change). That is real, deliberately out of scope — it is host state, and this task's own instructions say the toolbar takes callbacks, not an Editor. Whoever wires FocusControls into a real host (DomCanvas or ReactFlowHost) owns writing that host's own selection-to-seed and dimming-lens glue; scene/focus.ts's pure functions are what it should call.

Scope note distinguishing two SIMILAR but DIFFERENT SystemSketch features, since the vault conflates them nowhere but they are easy to confuse: this port is propagation FOCUS (a reading lens over the dataflow graph — 'what's near this'). depthNavigation.ts/depthBreadcrumbs.ts is a DIFFERENT feature (a drill-in stack — 'where am I in the nesting') and was read for orientation only, nothing from it was ported.

The vault has no existing 'focus view' section and no 'Focus View' menu entry yet (Zach: 'I should have a section in this obsidian vault for this focus view and in menus there can be the Focus View floating toolbar'). What DOES exist: Projects/bbox-ui/bbox ui Menus.md, a list of DP-<Name> component pages (Glyph Menu, Autocomplete Menu, Contextual Popup Menu, Toolbar, Inspector Panel) — a Focus View entry would follow that same convention (a new DP - Focus View page) if Zach wants one authored. Not created here: authoring a new DP page is a deliberate content decision, not a side effect of a code port, and the task's own instructions say to report this rather than silently invent taxonomy.

The donor's CSS-only dimming lens (propagation-focus.css's opacity(.17)/120ms rule, applied via a container data-attribute + MutationObserver so newly-mounted tldraw shapes stay dimmed while panning) was NOT ported as a reusable file — that dimming is host-paint, and this repo's hosts don't share a single DOM convention the way tldraw's .tl-shape[data-shape-id] does. The story fixture reproduces the same visual treatment (identical opacity .17 / 120ms ease-out values, cited inline) directly on its own Block/Trace wrappers as a worked example, not a shipped component.

propagationFocus.ts:266-345 (rootsFor/getPropagationFocusStepLimits/stepLimitsFor/snapshotFor)focus.ts's rootsForSeed/focusStepLimits/stepLimitsFor/focusSnapshotRe-expressed as POLICY, not code: same decision rules (a selected edge lights both endpoints; downstream's cap is measured against upstream's already-chosen range), but over a plain BlockScene + seed id instead of an Editor + TLShapeId — no shape lookups, no WeakMap store.
propagationFocus.ts's Editor-bound store: subscribePropagationFocus, startPropagationFocus, relationStoreFor's diff-driven cache, livePropagationEdges's canonical-connection admissionNot ported — stays host stateDeliberately out of scope: this is tldraw's own store subscription and connection-validity filter, not portable policy. A real host integration (React state, or a store keyed the same way) owns calling focus.ts's pure functions from its own selection/document state.
PropagationFocusControls.tsx (169 lines)editor/focusControls.tsxPorted as POLICY: same control shape (a "Focus" trigger, two independently-bounded ranges, a "Clear"), useEditor/useValue/useSyncExternalStore replaced by plain props/callbacks.
PropagationFocusControls.tsx:53-56's RTL WHY comment and its native dir="rtl" inputfocusControls.tsx's <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">Carried forward, mechanism changed. The donor's control is a native <input type="range">, so a bare dir attribute is enough — the browser does the reversal. The vendored shadcn Slider is a composed Base UI control (Root/Control/Track/Indicator/Thumb), which reads direction from React context, not the DOM dir attribute (confirmed by reading SliderControl.mjs/SliderThumb.mjs — both call useDirection() from @base-ui/react's own direction-context, and neither reads element.dir). DirectionProvider from @base-ui/react/direction-provider is the correct integration point; scoped to just the one Slider, matching the donor's own scope (its dir="rtl" sat on the <input> alone, never the wrapping <label>).
propagation-focus.css (76 lines)Not ported as a file — see FindingsHost-paint, reproduced inline in the story as a worked example instead of shipped as a reusable stylesheet.
